rationale: The aim is local improvement of an education process, with change ideas that need adapting between cycles. PDSA cycles with a weekly run chart fit the volume (about 45 forms a week), use a rating method that is reliable and quick (c2), and test changes with retrieved support (c1, c5) while building in the reinforcement that teaching alone lacks (c3). Reporting follows SQUIRE 2.0.
alternatives: Controlled comparison with another residency (refused: no partner programme and the question is local improvement)
Faculty teaching alone (refused: fades without reinforcement, claim c3)
Monitoring comment quality without any change (kept as the baseline period only)
whyNotMoreComplex: A controlled or cluster design would need several programmes and a fixed intervention; the run chart shows whether this residency improved and keeps the package adaptable.

decision.statement: Test the three-part change package in PDSA cycles from October 2026 to March 2027, with a weekly run chart of the proportion of 25 sampled comments meeting all three criteria, balancing measures for forms completed and timeliness, and a monthly breakdown by resident gender.
decision.question: Should the residency test prompts, micro-teaching and individual reports to raise actionable written feedback?

criteria.text: Each change idea has been followed by more actionable comments elsewhere and the rating method is reliable and quick.
The number of forms completed per week falls by more than a fifth during a cycle.

gates.requirement: Education research office determination that the project is quality improvement
gates.evidence: Determination EDU-QI-2026-19 dated 2026-08-05, supplied by the investigator
Program director approval PD-2026-08 dated 2026-08-18, supplied by the investigator

decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1, c2, c3 and c5 from retrieved records and on the investigator's approvals for both gates.

summary: QI with PDSA cycles recommended; the decision rests on four ledger claims and both gates are met.
